newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen property recovery seen in H1 97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen property recovery seen in H1 97 - paper.

text.p: The real estate market in the southern Chinese boomtown of Shenzhen showed signs of recovery in the first half of 1997 after a slump of more than three years, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
A total of 1.6 million square metres (17.2 million sq ft) of property was sold in Shenzhen in the first six months, a 35 percent increase on the year-ago period, the newspaper said.
Residential property accounted for 73.5 percent of the sales, indicating the slump that lasted three and a half years had ended, it said.
The value of the sales in the first half surged 1.78 billion yuan ($214.45 million) or 76.4 percent year-on-year to 4.11 billion yuan, indicating a rise in sale prices, it said.
The newspaper attributed the market revival to reduced property supply and stronger demand stimulated by the return to China on July 1 of the former British colony of Hong Kong.
Shenzhen had been attracting increasing numbers of residents from Hong Kong because of a gap in real estate prices in the two cities, analysts said.
Prices in Hong Kong are usually six to 10 times those in Shenzhen, they said.
Completed property in Shenzhen fell by 325,700 square metres (3.5 million sq ft) or 25.37 percent year-on-year to 958,000 sq m (10.3 million sq ft) in first-half 1997, the newspaper said.
Industry experts expected Shenzhen's property market to warm up further in the second half of the year, with prices and sales continuing to rise, it said.
"Years of consolidation have seen the Shenzhen property market bottomed out," the newspaper quoted Zheng Jiaguang, a senior official at the Shenzhen State Land Bureau, as saying.
"A recovery is bound to occur according to market forces," he said.
